title: Doing voluntary work
titleCn: 雅思听力Part2志愿工作经历与建议

paragraphs.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions eleven to sixteen.

Good evening. My name's Allen, and I'm so pleased to be here to talk to you about volunteering. With busy lives, it can be hard to find time to volunteer. However, the benefits of doing so are enormous to you, your family, and your community.

Let me start by telling you about my own experience. I've done various types of volunteering over the last few years. At the moment, for example, I spend every Saturday morning in our local folk museum. My earliest experience was when I was still at school, when I used to go to the hospital one evening a week to take a trolley of library books round the wards. I moved on from that to spending my university summer vacations helping out at a zoo. That was amazing fun.
My own decision to volunteer came as a result of a lesson at school when one of my classmates told us all about his holiday volunteering as a swimming pool lifeguard.

When I told my mother I wanted to do something similar the following summer, she suggested I got started a bit sooner than that. So the next day I asked our class teacher what other volunteering opportunities there might be for me, and that's what got me going.

There are many advantages to volunteering. Which you experience depends to some extent on the kind of activity you opt for, though of course, whatever you do, you can enjoy feeling you're making a valuable contribution to society. It may give you the opportunity to learn how to do all sorts of useful and interesting things. As far as I'm concerned, the key thing's been the joy of getting to know people who I wouldn't otherwise have had the chance to meet. I'm frequently asked whether there are any opportunities for doing voluntary work in your own home. There are a few, mainly involving writing, graphic design, or various types of handicraft. It obviously doesn't fit with everyone's lifestyle, but it amazes me how many people do opt for this route.

In general, there are lots of things to ask yourself when deciding what type of volunteering will be right for you. Most people know it's important to take their own skills into account. They know they need to think about whether they have what it takes to do the work they're considering. They're also aware of what it might mean in terms of hours and whether this will be possible for them, given any other commitments they may have.
But sometimes people don't give any thought to the degree of independence they'd like. For example, some people want to be in charge, while others prefer not to have to make decisions.

So what advice would I give about making the most of a volunteering experience? Well, the first thing I'd say is things may well not be quite what you expected, but stick at it. You'll find it's almost always possible to have fun. And that, after all, is also a valuable part of the point of getting involved in volunteering.
Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions seventeen to twenty.
Now listen and answer questions seventeen to twenty.
I'd like now to talk more specifically about a volunteer called Anna, who spent a year abroad volunteering on a Caribbean island.
At first, it was a culture shock, but she soon settled in and really enjoyed herself.

Anna got involved in different activities while she was abroad. She'd expected she'd probably be teaching on the island, but they were still building the school, so she was asked to be a nursing auxiliary at the local clinic. She got very good at taking blood pressures and temperatures.
She also helped with harvesting bananas at the farm where she was lodging, and another volunteer staying at the same place helped set up a library in the village.

Anna came back enormously enthusiastic about volunteering and wants to promote the idea. You may have read an interview she did with a reporter in the local paper about her voluntary work. If you'd like to read more about her experiences, then I'll give you the link for a wonderful site she's set up for school children who are considering volunteering. She's going to be talking about her experiences next month at a conference for people interested in volunteering, and any of you would be welcome to go to that too. Just have a word with me.
